spans.s: भिक्ष् vt. or vi. 1Ā (pres. भिक्षते) (This is one of those roots which take two accusatives, e.g. भिक्षमाणो वनं प्रियाम् Bt.vi.9.) 1. To ask, to ask for, to beg for; 2. to beg alms, यज्ञार्थमर्थं भिक्षित्वा यो न सर्वं प्रयच्छति M.xi.25; 3. to ask for without obtaining; 4. to be weary, to be distressed.
भिक्षण n. Asking alms, begging.
भिक्षणा f. Asking alms, begging.
भिक्षा f. 1. Asking, begging, M.vi.56; 2. anything given as alms; 3. wages, hire; 4. service.
भिक्षा-अटन (I) n. going about for alms.
भिक्षा-अटन (II) m. a mendicant.
भिक्षा-अन्न n. food obtained by alms.
भिक्षा-अयण n. going about for alms.
भिक्षा-अर्थिन् a. begging, asking for alms.
भिक्षा-अर्ह a. fit object of charity.
भिक्षा-आशिन् a. 1. subsisting on alms; 2. dishonest.
भिक्षा-आहार m. begged food.
भिक्षा-उपजीविन् a. subsisting on alms.
भिक्षा-करण n. begging, asking alms.
भिक्षा-चरण, -चर्य न्।, -चर्या ऋ। n. going about for alms.
भिक्षा-चरण, -चर्य न्।, -चर्या ऋ। n. going about for alms.
भिक्षा-चर्या f. going about for alms.
भिक्षा-पात्र, -भांड n. a vessel for collecting alms.
भिक्षा-पात्र, -भांड n. a vessel for collecting alms.
भिक्षा-माणव m. a young beggar (used contemptuously).
भिक्षा-वृत्ति f. living on alms.
भिक्षाक m. (fem. ˚की) A beggar, a mendicant.
भिक्षित a. (f. ता) Begged, solicited.
भिक्षित a. (f. ता) Begged, solicited.

भिक्षु m. 1. A begsrar, a mendicant in general, M.iii.94; 2. a Buddhist mendicant; 3. the fourth order in the religious life of a Brāhmaṇa (संन्यास); 4. a Brāhmaṇa in the fourth order of his life (संन्यासिन्).
भिक्षु-चर्या f. the life of a mendicant.
भिक्षु-संघ m. a society of Buddhist mendicants.
भिक्षु-संघाती f. old clothes.
भिक्षुक m. A beggar, a mendicant, Yaj.iii.59.
